channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: É #FAKE que eleições de 2026 terão novo modelo de urna eletrônica
item.description: The TSE denies that new electronic voting machines will be adopted for the 2026 elections, stating that the models currently in use — UE2022, UE2020, UE2015, and UE2013 — will continue to be deployed, with identical technical functionality despite design differences. The development of the next-generation UE2028 model is underway via public consultation and will be used starting in the 2028 municipal elections. The false claim spread on social media, alleging new machines, source-code audits, and international presence, was debunked by the TSE.

item.title: Convidado por Caiado para ministério, Gakiya diverge de candidato quanto a classificar PCC e CV como terroristas
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, presidential candidate from the PSD, advocates classifying PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, following the U.S. designation, and included this in his government plan, including a proposed Domestic Terrorism Law. In contrast, Lincoln Gakiya, a São Paulo prosecutor known for his work against the PCC, disagrees with Caiado, warning that the classification threatens Brazilian sovereignty, hinders international information sharing, and could trigger economic sanctions, despite his history of confronting the faction.

item.title: Os (poucos) 45 dias que decidem o Brasil
item.description: Brazilian electoral law restricts official campaigning to just 45 days before the first round, an insufficient period for adequate deliberation on government proposals affecting 215 million people. This reduction, stemming from the 2015 mini-reform, aimed to cut costs and abuses but has undermined the quality of public debate, unlike in other democracies where electoral processes are longer and more structured. As a result, voters are overwhelmed by a disordered avalanche of information, making informed choices difficult in state, legislative, and presidential elections.

item.title: Lula de chapéu: caso de deputado do PT abriu precedente no TSE para foto com adereço na urna; entenda
item.description: Lula's campaign used a photo of him wearing a Panama hat for the 2026 elections, which may raise questions at the TSE regarding accessory use in ballot images, despite a 2022 precedent allowing Douglas Belchior to wear a cap as part of his cultural identity. Electoral rules prohibit adornments but permit ethnic/religious attire and disability-related accessories. The TSE will assess whether the hat constitutes cultural identity or mere ornamentation.

item.title: Michelle sai da crise com Flávio como personagem disputada por candidatos do PL e consolida capital político
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro overcame her rift with Flávio Bolsonaro and solidified her political capital, now being courted by PL and allied candidates for photos and campaign support, particularly for Senate races. Her work with PL Mulher and the nationwide network she built reinforced her autonomy and influence within bolsonarism, despite earlier efforts to downplay her role. The shift in allies’ behavior — from critics to seekers of her image — demonstrates that she preserved her independent electoral asset.

item.title: De olho na eleição, Lula se reaproxima de Alcolumbre e Motta para aprovar pautas antes do primeiro turno
item.description: The Lula government has intensified dialogue with House Speaker Arthur Lira and Senate President Rodrigo Pacheco to advance priority agendas, such as the PEC ending the 6x1 workweek, before the first round of the 2026 elections, using them as campaign showcases. The strategy also aims to secure their support for Lula’s re-election, while they seek his backing to retain leadership of Congress in the next term.

item.title: Com novo marqueteiro, Flávio prepara largada doméstica após desgastes com Milei e Trump e mira evangélicos
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) launches his presidential campaign with a domestic-focused agenda under new communications chief Duda Lima, following distractions tied to Javier Milei and Donald Trump. The strategy emphasizes outreach to evangelical leaders, Southeastern Brazil tours (60% of agenda), and core issues like security, inflation, employment, and criticism of Lula’s government, while preserving Bolsonarist base appeal without external distractions. The campaign also enlisted 47 Senate candidates as regional multipliers to expand reach across Brazil’s limited 40-day campaign window.

item.title: Fiscal de subprefeitura é flagrado panfletando para vereadora do União
item.description: A contracts inspector from the Vila Mariana Subprefecture was caught distributing political flyers for councilwoman Amanda Vettorazzo (União) during his day off, according to his statement. The employee, affiliated with the MBL and campaign coordinator for presidential candidate Renan Santos (Missão), denied acting during work hours and claimed the activity was a legitimate exercise of his political rights. The subprefecture is described as a stronghold of MBL and Missão party members, with former subprefect Rafael Minatogawa also running for state deputy under the same party.

item.title: De olho em Minas, Lula e Flávio visitam estado na largada da campanha
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) are visiting Minas Gerais to launch the campaigns of their gubernatorial candidates: Flávio Roscoe (PL) and Patrus Ananias (PT), respectively. The visits come amid a tight race in the state, which has over 16 million voters and is considered pivotal for the presidential election. The presence of the presidential contenders underscores the strategic importance of Minas Gerais in the 2026 electoral contest.

item.title: Audiência da GloboNews cresce com entrevistas de candidatos à Presidência
item.description: GloboNews led news channel ratings on paid TV during three days of presidential candidate interviews, achieving 35.5% higher viewership than the average of the previous four weeks. Over 1.1 million people watched the interviews on 'Estúdio i', conducted by Andréia Sadi and Natuza Nery with Renan Santos (Mission), Romeu Zema (Novo) and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD). Lula da Silva and Flávio did not participate despite being invited.

item.title: Entenda como a disputa ao Senado virou central nas eleições deste ano
item.description: The Senate race has become central in the 2026 elections, with 54 of 81 seats up for grabs due to the renewal of two-thirds of the chamber. Parties are seeking a majority to control the legislative agenda, influence the Executive, and potentially affect the composition of the STF, as removing a minister requires two-thirds senatorial approval. The outcome will determine whether the Senate leans left or right, directly impacting presidential governability.

item.title: A atuação de Tarcísio para manter Cleitinho na disputa em Minas
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas worked behind the scenes to keep Senator Cleitinho as the Republicanos party's candidate for Minas Gerais governor in 2026, including calls to the party's national president. Cleitinho had fluctuated on his candidacy, announcing withdrawal before reversing course after national party lobbying, which impacted internal party polling.

item.title: Pra que lado aponta o pêndulo do Centrão? - O Assunto #1781
item.description: After years of tension with the Lula government, the Centrão bloc is shifting its stance ahead of the 2026 elections, announcing neutrality in the presidential race and avoiding alignment with Flávio Bolsonaro. Chamber President Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB) declared support for Lula’s re-election, following a renewed dialogue between Lula and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) after months of no communication. Journalist Bela Megale reveals the behind-the-scenes dynamics, suggesting a move from confrontation to a potential governability arrangement, though the long-term future of the Executive-Legislative relationship remains uncertain.

item.title: ‘Bondade’ eleitoreira de Lula resulta em má gestão da dívida
item.description: President Lula’s electoral-era credit and loan measures injected R$149 billion (1.1% of GDP) into the economy in the first half of 2024 alone, according to BRCG consulting firm. This amount nearly matches the total of similar measures granted throughout 2023, raising concerns about fiscal mismanagement and rising public debt. The full report is available only to GLOBO subscribers.

item.title: Câmara instala comissão sobre redução da maioridade penal, mas proposta deve ficar para depois das eleições
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies installs this Wednesday a special commission to discuss reducing the age of criminal responsibility, chaired by Aluísio Mendes (Republicanos-MA) and with Mendonça Filho (PL-PE) as rapporteur. Although installed, work will effectively begin in September, with a vote on the report expected between late November and early December, after the elections, per an agreement with Chamber President Hugo Motta. The proposal is supported by right-wing lawmakers but faces opposition due to concerns over early incarceration and doubts about its effectiveness in reducing crime.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Quanto ganham presidente, deputados e senadores?
item.description: In Brazil, the President, 513 federal deputies, 81 senators, 11 STF ministers, and 38 state ministers all receive the same gross salary of R$ 46,366.00, which is the public service ceiling. This amount is fixed by law and does not include cabinet allowances or parliamentary quotas, which are for official duties and not personal income. Exceptions to the ceiling, such as pension accumulation with office, are excluded from this survey.

item.title: Candidato tem que declarar tudo o que possui? Entenda as regras da declaração de bens nas eleições
item.description: The asset declaration is a mandatory requirement for candidacy registration, allowing voters to consult the assets declared by candidates. It must include real estate, vehicles, financial investments, stocks, and company participations, without requiring location details for security reasons. The declared value does not need to reflect current market price and may be based on historical cost; salaries and income are not included in the declaration.

item.title: Congresso instala hoje comissão para analisar MP que acabou com taxas das blusinhas
item.description: The National Congress today installed a mixed committee to analyze the provisional measure that ends the 'blusinhas tax' (20% charge on international purchases), a measure criticized by retailers and seen as electoral. The text must be voted by September 8 to remain valid, and Lula’s allies fear Congress will let the MP expire to harm the president one month before the 2026 elections.

item.title: Planalto aprecia gesto de Alcolumbre de instalar comissão para analisar MP que acaba com taxa das blusinhas
item.description: The Lula government welcomed Senate President Davi Alcolumbre’s move to install a committee to analyze the MP ending the 'blusinhas tax,' but objected to Eduardo Braga’s appointment as rapporteur due to his ties to the Manaus Free Trade Zone and fears he might benefit the region during the election campaign. The government is seeking an alternative rapporteur before the MP expires on September 8, as its lapse would reinstate the 20% import tax on purchases under US$50 — a risk that could take effect less than a month before the October 4, 2026, first-round election.

item.title: Michelle expõe feridas ao aceitar gravar vídeo de campanha com Flávio dois meses após racha público
item.description: Former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro met with Flávio Bolsonaro to record campaign videos, marking their first in-person contact since publicly reconciling after a June rift. The meeting took place on Tuesday (11) and underscores efforts to unite the Bolsonaro family ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Candidatos ao Senado por SP têm encontros com agro, artistas e Flávio
item.description: Senate candidates from São Paulo, including Simone Tebet (PSB) and Marina Silva (Rede), met with cultural and artistic representatives at Teatro Oficina, advocating for culture as an educational priority and a tool to reduce violence. Ricardo Salles (Novo) attended a bioenergy fair in Sertãozinho with agribusiness figures, alongside Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), though he denied substantive talks. The bill to regulate and tax streaming platforms (VOD), approved by the CCS, now awaits Senate vote.

item.title: "Não usei carteira de advogado para mim, mas usei para o Lula", brinca Haddad
item.description: Fernando Haddad, São Paulo gubernatorial candidate and former Finance Minister, joked that he did not use his OAB lawyer's license for himself but 'for Lula', during a magna lecture at USP on superindustrial capitalism. He recalled his legal career and said he keeps the license as a precaution in a 'complicated' country. The remark came while discussing his 2025 book analyzing how automation, AI, and economic power concentration are transforming labor, production models, and state challenges.

item.title: O recado de contrariedade de Michelle mesmo depois de gravar vídeos de campanha com Flávio
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro and Flávio Bolsonaro met to record campaign videos, attempting to project an image of reconciliation after a public conflict, but the encounter was described by reporter Nicholas Shores as 'highly scripted' and 'cinematic.' Despite Michelle claiming they had 'put a stone over the disagreement' and spoken of 'turning the page,' she publicly reiterated the same positions that caused the rift, particularly her visceral opposition to an alliance with Ciro Gomes in Ceará and her complaint about lacking autonomy in selecting Senate candidates for PL Mulher.

item.title: Alcolumbre indica trégua com Lula no Senado
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) decided to end his feud with President Lula and resumed contact with the Planalto Palace last week. The rapprochement is based on the possible nomination of Senator Rodrigo Pacheco (PSB-MG) to a vacancy at the Federal Court of Accounts (TCU), should a position become available.

item.title: Motta cria oficialmente comissão da PEC que reduz maioridade penal
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta formally established the special committee to analyze the PEC lowering the criminal age of majority from 18 to 16. The committee's installation is scheduled for Wednesday (12/8), with Aluisio Mendes expected as president and Mendonça Filho as rapporteur. Despite progress in committees, leaders anticipate difficulties in bringing the proposal to the plenary before the October elections, given the sensitive nature of the issue in an election year.

item.title: Lula usa chapéu pela primeira vez em foto de urna; TSE flexibilizou regra sobre acessório em 2022
item.description: Lula registered his ballot photo with the TSE for the 2026 elections, wearing a hat for the first time due to medical recommendations following head surgeries and skin cancer treatment. Although electoral rules prohibit adornments in ballot photos, the TSE relaxed this rule in 2022, allowing accessories that represent identity or have medical justification, as in Lula's case. The hat is a Panama model from Sarquis by ABA, used since October 2024 to protect the operated area.

item.title: Governo Lula provocou tarifaço, diz candidato do PL em Minas Gerais
item.description: Flávio Roscoe, PL candidate for governor of Minas Gerais, criticized the Lula government for worsening the trade crisis with the United States through misguided demonstrations and gratuitous provocations, harming dialogue and Brazilian industry. He argues Brazil missed a chance to maintain a negotiation channel with the Trump administration and that the conflict may have been used to divert attention from domestic problems.

item.title: Suplente destinou R$ 11,6 milhões a redutos de Josimar Maranhãozinho
item.description: While serving as a substitute member of the Chamber of Deputies in 2024, Paulo Marinho Jr. (PL-MA) directed R$ 11.6 million in parliamentary amendments to cities linked to Josimar Maranhãozinho (PL-MA), including municipalities governed by his relatives and allies, such as Zé Doca (his sister), Maranhãozinho (his political base), and Centro do Guilherme (his wife). Josimar is under investigation by the Federal Police for embezzlement of amendments, raising suspicions of public funds being used to strengthen electoral strongholds.

item.title: 'Centros-dia' para idosos são elogiados, mas debate na CDH alerta para custo
item.description: The CDH public hearing debated PL 5.115/2025, proposing nationwide day-care centers for the elderly within SUAS, praised for promoting dignity and reducing isolation, but raising concerns about budgetary impact on municipalities and the need for explicit federal funding.

item.title: Tarcísio critica falta de subsídio federal a produtores de cana de SP
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas criticized the federal subsidy announced for sugarcane producers in the Northeast, arguing that São Paulo producers were overlooked despite also suffering losses from U.S. tariffs and extreme weather. He highlighted a tax imbalance that undermines the competitiveness of São Paulo’s sugarcane sector, particularly relative to corn ethanol in other states. The R$12-per-ton subsidy, capped at R$270 million, was formalized in Decree No. 13.092/2026 and applies to the 2025/2026 harvest.

item.title: La esposa y el hijo de Bolsonaro escenifican su reconciliación a las puertas de las elecciones en Brasil
item.description: Wife Michelle and son Flávio Bolsonaro appear together in Brasília to symbolize family reconciliation after public accusations of disrespect and humiliation. The meeting takes place ahead of the 2026 elections, featuring campaign video recordings and joint prayer at the Liberal Party headquarters. The gesture aims to project Bolsonaro clan unity amid the electoral challenge.

item.title: Plano de segurança de Lula repete promessas feitas em 2002 que não foram cumpridas em 24 anos
item.description: Lula's 2026 security plan repeats promises made in 2002, such as police unification, community policing, and favela urbanization, many of which remain unfulfilled after 24 years. Although some initiatives like the Integrated Forces to Combat Organized Crime have been introduced, the document states that half of the original 28 proposals remain unmet, including the effective establishment of a Unified Public Security System. The central criticism is that the current plan appears to be a copy of the 2002 version, lacking significant progress in reducing violence or combating corruption within security forces.

item.title: Entidades citam 'ameaça à liberdade de imprensa' após busca autorizada por Moraes contra fonte de jornalista no Maranhão
item.description: Press organizations criticized Justice Alexandre de Moraes' decision to authorize a search and seizure operation against the source of a Maranhão journalist, calling it a serious threat to press freedom and a violation of constitutional source protection. The operation targeted Raimundo Cutrim, former Maranhão government secretary, suspected of providing information to journalist Luis Pablo about Flávio Dino's use of an official vehicle. The ANJ, Abert, and Aner stated that violating source confidentiality lacks constitutional basis and sets dangerous precedents for democracy.

item.title: Senado aprova plano para fabricação de fertilizantes no Brasil
item.description: The Senate approved Bill 699/2023, establishing the Fertilizer Industry Development Program (Profert), which includes tax incentives and a fund to reduce Brazil’s reliance on fertilizer imports. The bill provides tax exemptions for machinery and supports the construction of domestic fertilizer plants to strengthen national agricultural input sovereignty. It now awaits presidential sanction after being passed by symbolic vote.

item.title: Lula liga para agradecer declaração de voto de Motta e o convida para encontro nesta semana
item.description: President Lula called Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta to thank him for his support in Lula's re-election bid and invited him to an in-person meeting this week. Motta's backing was key to keeping the Republicans party neutral in the election, preventing a shift toward supporting Flávio Bolsonaro. The move reflects broader political maneuvering in Paraíba, where Lula is also backing Veneziano Vital do Rêgo and João Azevedo for Senate, despite Motta's father, Nabor Wanderley, running as a Republican candidate.

item.title: Novo fundo para promover acesso à Justiça gratuita vai à sanção
item.description: The Senate approved a bill to create the Access to Justice Strengthening Fund for the Federal Public Defender's Office, aiming to provide free and comprehensive legal aid to low-income individuals. The fund will be financed through budget allocations, judicial fees, proceeds from abandoned assets, and parliamentary amendments, with explicit prohibitions on using resources for indemnities or personnel expenses except in specific cases. The bill now awaits presidential sanction after being approved by symbolic vote.

item.title: Daniel Vilela declara R$ 5,6 milhões ao TSE; vice informa R$ 10,4 milhões
item.description: Governor candidate Daniel Vilela (MDB) declared R$ 5.6 million in assets to the TSE, a 19.8% increase from 2022. His running mate, Luiz Carlos do Carmo (PMDB), reported R$ 10.4 million, up 33% since 2018. Together, their declared assets total R$ 16.1 million, including loan credits and business holdings.

item.title: MPE acusa candidato ao Senado de fraude por usar sobrenome Bolsonaro
item.description: The Electoral Public Ministry of Rondônia is seeking to invalidate the candidacy of Bruno Scheid (PL) for using the ballot name 'Bruno Bolsonaro Scheid' without having the surname Bolsonaro in his civil name, claiming it misleads voters and constitutes electoral fraud. The MPE alleges the candidate is gaining electoral advantage by falsely implying a familial link to Jair Bolsonaro, which is untrue, and that the improper use of the surname had already been sanctioned by electoral justice. Although the Rondônia Regional Electoral Court previously rejected similar injunction requests, the MPE now argues that registering the ballot name itself constitutes an electoral violation.

item.title: O impacto das suspeitas sobre Marcola e Lulinha na campanha de Lula à reeleição
item.description: The Democracia em Xeque Institute's study finds that suspicions surrounding Lulinha and Marcola do not significantly damage Lula's image, as voters perceive the allegations as vague and lacking direct ties to the president. However, these cases remain important vulnerabilities, increasing pressure on Lula to be more cautious in selecting close associates and to preserve investigative autonomy. Lula gains support among undecided voters when he avoids turning family suspicions into political spectacle and maintains a calm, reserved demeanor.

item.title: Pivô de racha entre Michelle e Flávio triplica patrimônio em dois anos
item.description: Federal deputy André Fernandes (PL-CE), who played a central role in the dispute between Michelle and Flávio Bolsonaro, saw his declared assets to the TSE triple in two years, rising from R$ 377,705 in 2024 to R$ 1,203,754.67 in 2026. The substantial increase raises questions about the origin of the funds, particularly given his recent political activity.

item.title: Quem são os candidatos ao Senado por São Paulo (SP) nas Eleições 2026
item.description: Ten candidates have been confirmed to run for the two Senate seats from São Paulo in the 2026 elections. Eight of them are already registered in the TSE’s candidacy and finance system, while two others were formalized in party conventions but are still awaiting official registration. The race reflects national political polarization, with candidates from diverse ideological spectrums competing for representation in the Federal Senate.

item.title: Luis César Bueno declara R$ 884 mil ao TSE; vice informa R$ 328 mil
item.description: Luis César Bueno, the PT candidate for governor of Goiás, declared R$ 884 thousand in assets to the TSE, including a house valued at R$ 516 thousand and a car at R$ 170 thousand. His running mate, Carlos Mundim (PDT), declared R$ 328.6 thousand, with R$ 212 thousand in cash and R$ 100 thousand in a business stake. Both are first-time candidates for statewide executive office in 2026.

item.title: Candidata a deputada, Silvia Abravanel declara patrimônio de 47,5 milhões de reais
item.description: Silvia Abravanel, daughter of Silvio Santos and federal deputy candidate for the PSD in São Paulo, declared a net worth of R$ 47,546,965.91 according to the TSE. Her main assets include a Santander LCI investment (R$ 17.25 million), a R$ 7.5 million mansion, Bahamas-based shares (R$ 4.78 million), and judicial deposits tied to the ITCMD tax (R$ 9.31 million).

item.title: Lula liga para Motta e agradece apoio à reeleição
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) called House Speaker Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB) on Tuesday, March 11, to thank him for his support for Lula’s re-election bid. Motta had announced on Monday, March 10, that the Republicanos party’s Paraíba chapter would back Lula in the 2026 presidential election, stating that the trend in the state favors the incumbent. The call underscores Lula’s efforts to strengthen political alliances ahead of the 2026 race.

item.title: “Decisões ilegais não se cumprem”, diz Renan Santos
item.description: Presidential candidate Renan Santos criticized a decision by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes authorizing a search and seizure against Raimundo Cutrim, former Maranhão state secretary, linked to reporting on Minister Flávio Dino. Santos stated that 'illegal decisions are not to be obeyed,' challenging the ruling's legality.

item.title: Vice de Zema, Eduardo Girão se licencia do Senado por 121 dias
item.description: Senator Eduardo Girão (Novo-CE) took a 121-day leave from office to focus on his campaign as vice-presidential candidate on Romeu Zema's (Novo) ticket. His substitute, Sargento Reginauro (PSDB-CE), assumed the seat and disclosed he is undergoing cancer treatment following a bone marrow transplant. Girão, previously considered for governor of Ceará, described his candidacy as an 'existential mission' to combat the 'untouchables' of the STF and promote security, prosperity, and defense of life and family.

item.title: PF pede a Moraes definição sobre armas apreendidas de Bolsonaro
item.description: The Federal Police asked Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes to decide the fate of 10 firearms, ammunition, and accessories linked to former President Jair Bolsonaro, as the seizure was carried out under a judicial order, not a PF investigation. The items include restricted and permitted weapons, such as a customized shotgun with Brazil’s flag colors, and remain in PF custody pending Moraes’ ruling.

item.title: Patrimônio de líder do PL na Câmara cresce de R$7,7 mil para R$ 600 mil em quatro anos
item.description: The net worth of federal deputy Sóstenes Cavalcante (PL-RJ), leader of the PL in the Chamber, rose from R$ 7,7 thousand in 2022 to R$ 600 thousand in 2026, according to his TSE declaration. He claims the increase aligns with his annual salary of about R$ 600 thousand, totaling R$ 2.4 million over four years. The declared assets include R$ 500 thousand in cash — linked by the Federal Police to a suspected parliamentary fund diversion scheme — and a R$ 100 thousand plot in Brasília, though the deputy insists the funds came from a property sale.

item.title: Motta cancela sessão da Câmara após líder do PT passar mal em reunião
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta canceled Tuesday's voting session after PT leader Deputy Pedro Uczai fainted and had a seizure during a leadership meeting. Medical leaders provided first aid, and Uczai was treated and released conscious. The meeting aimed to set the agenda, including bills to reduce fuel taxes using oil revenues, incentivize fertilizer production, explore rare earths, and grant tax exemptions tied to the Women's World Cup.

item.title: Michelle passou de madrasta má a atração da campanha de Flávio
item.description: Flávio and Michelle Bolsonaro resumed communication after nearly two months of silence, following a public feud and reconciliation via social media. On Tuesday, they met in person and recorded videos for electoral propaganda, marking Michelle’s return as a central figure in the campaign.
